teams.heading: Fiji fall to late Samisoni Tua try in Pacific Nations Cup final
teams.body: Fiji failed to secure a third consecutive Pacific Nations Cup title on Saturday, falling 20-15 to Japan in a tense final in Tokyo. Despite first-half tries from Virimi Vakatawa and Tevita Ikanivere giving the Flying Fijians a 12-10 lead at the interval, the side struggled after Mesake Doge received a yellow card. Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula kicked a penalty to level the scores at 15-15, but a late Samisoni Tua try sealed the victory for Eddie Jones’ men.

lead.why: Fiji suffered a narrow 20-15 defeat to Japan in the Pacific Nations Cup final on Saturday.

teams.heading: England women draw with Canada to close 39-match unbeaten run
teams.body: England’s remarkable 39-match winning streak concluded on Friday as the Red Roses were held to a 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park. Despite the stalemate ending their perfect run, John Mitchell’s side extended their unbeaten sequence to 40 Tests in a physical encounter. England led through tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, Hannah Botterman, and Bryony Field, but were unable to convert late pressure into a victory. Mitchell remained optimistic, stating, "I'm a realist. There will be greater things come as a result of this."

lead.why: England's women's team ended a historic 39-game winning streak following a hard-fought draw against Canada.

teams.heading: France implements protected player list to target 2027 World Cup success
teams.body: The French Rugby Federation has officially introduced a 'protected player list' of 33 individuals to manage workloads ahead of the 2027 World Cup. Under this new agreement with Top 14 clubs, these players will be granted a weekend off every 4 matches to mitigate injury risks. In exchange, these stars are restricted to a total of 9 Test matches during the upcoming international windows. The list reportedly features 13 players from Toulouse, including Antoine Dupont, Romain Ntamack, and Thomas Ramos.

teams.heading: Jemima Adams Verling earns debut as Ireland faces United States today
teams.body: Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling will make her senior Ireland debut in the WXV Global Series opener. Head coach Scott Bemand has selected the 20-year-old at blind-side flanker alongside captain Erin King and Aoife Wafer in the back row. This fixture marks the start of a new three-year cycle as the squad builds toward the next World Cup. Bemand stated that the series represents a "turning of the page" for the team as they look to develop greater depth.

teams.heading: Scotland struggle as New Zealand run in 10 tries at Hive
teams.body: Scotland suffered a 66-14 defeat to New Zealand at Hive Stadium on Saturday, marking a second successive loss in the WXV Global Series. Despite Evie Gallagher scoring two first-half tries to keep the hosts in contention, the world’s second-ranked side proved too clinical, securing 10 tries in total. The Black Ferns dominated the contest, effectively ending the game as a competition by half-time. Scotland now turn their attention to facing Australia at the same venue next Saturday.

teams.heading: Wales Women destroy South Africa in stunning eight-try WXV opening victory
teams.body: Wales secured a dominant 50-19 win over South Africa in their WXV Global Series opener at Cardiff Arms Park. Sean Lynn’s side raced to a 38-5 half-time lead, with Sisilia Tuipulotu scoring twice and co-captain Alex Callender earning player of the match honours. After a nine-test winless streak, the performance signalled a new direction for the squad. "This is just the start for us, this is going to be our new DNA," said Lynn following the emphatic victory.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones’ Japan defeat Fiji to secure Pacific Nations Cup title
teams.body: Japan claimed the Pacific Nations Cup with a 20-15 victory over Fiji in Tokyo on Saturday. After previous final losses to the Flying Fijians, Eddie Jones’ side secured the win with a decisive 70th-minute try from Samisoni Tua. Flanker Ben Gunter also crossed, while Mamoru Harada provided an earlier score. Jones noted that the result offers a platform for the squad, stating: “It’s a great opportunity for this team to grow.” The victory concludes a successful campaign for the hosts.

lead.why: Japan's victory in the Pacific Nations Cup final is the most significant competitive result for the team.
